body.statement: \(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G)=G^\star\) and \(\mathcal I_E(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G))=\mathcal I_E(G)\), where \(\operatorname{Adm}(G)\) ranges over all absent directed edges and unordered bidirected edges, including both loop types, even when additions jointly change SCCs and create previously unoccupied bidirected rectangles.
body.justification: It turns global closure into edgewise saturation.
body.gap: Individual safety does not generally imply joint safety.
body.consumer: An oracle algorithm tests only one-edge additions.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove that the union of all individually admissible profile-changing edges is E-equivalent to the base graph.
obligation.obstruction: Individual admissibility and antitonicity do not by themselves imply joint admissibility.  The exact equality with the unrestricted greatest representative needs the still-open union-closure theorem.
obligation.attempted: Singleton composition identifies each individually admissible edge with an E-equivalent one-edge extension \(G+e\), and the interval property identifies every edge of a hypothetical greatest member as admissible.  This yields the exact conditional formula but not unconditional simultaneous safety.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditionally on the greatest-representative theorem, one obtains the exact computable identity
\[
\operatorname{Adm}(G)=E(G^\star)\setminus E(G),
\qquad
G+\operatorname{Adm}(G)=G^\star.
\]
The forward inclusion uses singleton composition to put each \(G+e\) in the E-class; the reverse inclusion uses \(G\subseteq G+e\subseteq G^\star\) and antitonicity.  This proves the target for every fixed-profile family with \(G^\star\) replaced by its proved greatest member \(\Gamma(G)\), but the unrestricted statement still depends on the open transfer theorem.
